content.title: Ruth's Chris Steak House Says 'Proper Attire Required' in Dress Code Notice
content.text: The reminder comes after the chain joined restaurant giant Darden Restaurants in a $715 million acquisition A Ruth's Chris restaurant in Washington, D.C. Credit : Andrew Harrer/Bloomberg/Getty NEED TO KNOW Ruth’s Chris Steak House reminds diners hats are not allowed in dining roomsThe steakhouse asks guests to follow a “business casual” dress code policyThe chain has operated under Darden Restaurants since a $715 million acquisition in 2023 Diners heading to their nearest Ruth’s Chris Steak House may want to think twice before topping off their outfit with a baseball cap. The upscale steakhouse chain is reminding guests that its dining rooms maintain a “business casual” dress code — and that hats are not allowed at the table. According to a notice posted on the restaurant’s website, guests are asked to remove hats upon entering. Those wearing ball caps may instead be directed to dine in the bar or lounge area rather than the main dining room. The dining room at a Ruth's Chris in Houston. Michael Paulsen / Houston Chronicle/Getty The message also outlines clothing that is not permitted in dining rooms. “Business casual — proper attire required please,” the notice reads. The restaurant’s policy states that gym wear, pool attire, tank tops, clothing with offensive graphics or language, revealing clothing and exposed undergarments are not allowed inside dining rooms. It’s unclear when the notice was last updated, but the policy is currently visible on the restaurant’s website. The dress code reminder comes as the brand operates under new ownership. In 2023, restaurant giant Darden Restaurants — the company behind chains like Olive Garden and LongHorn Steakhouse — acquired Ruth’s Chris’ parent company in a deal valued at roughly $715 million, according to the Associated Press. “Ruth’s Chris is a strong and distinctive brand in the fine dining segment with an impressive history of delivering elevated dining experiences to their loyal guests,” Darden CEO Rick Cardenas said at the time of the announcement. Related Stories PEOPLE reached out to Ruth's Chris and Darden for further comment on the dress code requirements. The original Chris Steak House opened in New Orleans in 1927 and was later purchased by Ruth Fertel in 1965, who renamed it Ruth’s Chris Steak House. Today, the brand operates locations around the world. While Ruth’s Chris asks guests to follow a specific dress code, other restaurants within the Darden portfolio have slightly different policies. For example, The Capital Grille also encourages upscale attire but does not explicitly ban hats, though it warns against athletic wear and overly revealing clothing.
